question: Veer bought some pens at the rate of ₹180/dozen. He sold them for ₹22 each. His profit percentage is ______% (rounded off to two decimal places).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of 1 pen = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

SP of 1 pen = ₹22

Profit = 22 − 15 = ₹7

Profit % = (7 ÷ 15) × 100 = 140 ÷ 3 = 46.66...% ≈ 46.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 46.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of 1 dozen pens (12 pens) = ₹180

Selling price of 1 pen = ₹22

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 CP ₹15 SP ₹22 
• 
 Profit = ₹7 + 46.67% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost price of 1 pen = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

⇒ Selling price of 1 pen = ₹22

⇒ Profit = 22 − 15 = ₹7

⇒ Profit % = (7 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 700 ÷ 15

⇒ Profit % = 140 ÷ 3

⇒ Profit % = 46.66...% ≈ 46.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 46.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Cost Price (CP) is greater than Selling Price (SP), Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer claims to sell goods at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
